title: Peris unit production references
purpose: Research and production guidance for an infantry and cavalry prototype before expanding the faction roster.
recommendation: Create, fit, rig, texture, and inspect the source units in Blender. Deliver optimized GLB assets to the existing Three.js battle renderer.

sourcePack.author: Wildfire Games
sourcePack.usage: Licensed source study and adapted prototypes. Redistributed source assets and their adaptations require Wildfire Games attribution, the author and license links, and CC BY-SA 3.0 licensing.

observations.finding: The horse actor attaches a separate rider to its rider socket and adds blanket, chest band, and reins as props.
The rider actor uses separate head, helmet, shield, weapon, and cape attachments, plus mounted animation variants.
The infantry actor reuses a body mesh with separate equipment and action/formation variants.

workflow.title: Approve the silhouette
workflow.action: Use a licensed base with coherent anatomy. Build an original Peris identity through proportions, armor, cloth, weapons, and faction motifs. Inspect one infantry unit and one mounted unit from the game camera before building the roster.
workflow.basis: Peris production proposal informed by the art references.

workflow.title: Build a modular rig
workflow.action: Share compatible skeletons within a body family. Fit equipment to named attachments. Check joint deformation in action poses.

workflow.title: Treat cavalry as a complete assembly
workflow.action: Fit pelvis to saddle, thighs around the horse, boots to stirrups where present, and hands to reins or weapon grips. Use a rider attachment and a shared animation clock; verify idle, locomotion, and attack from side and front views. Retain compatible horse and rider clips rather than placing a standing soldier above a horse.
workflow.basis: The attachment is observed in 0 A.D.; the pose and synchronization checks are the proposed Peris workflow.

workflow.title: Author materials for the game
workflow.action: Use UV textures for base color, normal detail, and metallic/roughness response. Keep metal, skin, leather, and cloth distinct under neutral lighting. Adapt the downloaded legacy specular materials deliberately; a specular image is not automatically a metallic or roughness map.
workflow.basis: glTF material model plus the proposed conversion and visual checks for Peris.

workflow.title: Export a controlled GLB
workflow.action: Preserve the editable Blender source. Export the intended unit collection, including the skin and named animation clips. Inspect the result, optimize a separate output, validate it, and compare it in Three.js with the source appearance.
workflow.basis: Three.js supports GLB skins and animation clips; the source preservation and validation sequence is the proposed Peris workflow.

workflow.title: Render armies within a measured budget
workflow.action: Share compatible assets, cull offscreen soldiers, and reduce distant detail. After validating individual clips, consider bone animation textures with per-instance timing. Measure armies on named hardware.
workflow.basis: NVIDIA's DirectX 10 technique requires adaptation and measurements in Three.js/WebGL.

reviewCriteria: Anatomy and equipment read clearly from the battle camera.
Rider contacts stay believable throughout idle, movement, and attack clips.
Clips and attachments survive export with no missing textures or broken bind pose.
The optimized asset visually matches the accepted source at each detail level.
Full-army measurements record hardware, viewport, unit count, quality, FPS, draw calls, and triangles.
Existing formation commands, combat rules, and saved game behavior remain independently verified.

prototypes.status: First Roman infantry and seated cavalry prototypes are available for visual review in the playable battle preview.
prototypes.preservation: Use an unused edition name for a new assembly. The builder refuses to overwrite existing editable sources. The review script saves a separate side-by-side scene under artifacts.
prototypes.limitations: The remaining faction roles retain the procedural prototype art. Siege studies are visual only; Academy research and Workshop recruitment are still design work. On Intel Iris Xe, Ultra at 1600x1000 averaged 56.7 FPS for twenty cavalry visible and 19.5 FPS for the full 540-soldier overview, with long stalls. Full-army performance still needs optimization.

status: First two licensed prototypes integrated; continuing visual review and faction art development.
